sections.html:
Brenham is the place to file. The Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, takes real property documents and acts as county recorder for the whole county. A deed for a house in Chappell Hill, Burton, Independence or Gay Hill goes to the same Brenham office as a deed for a house in Brenham itself.

The office phone, 979-277-6216, is the way to ask about hours and walk-in service. Probate filings, posted foreclosure notices and notices of state tax liens are kept there as well.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, releases, affidavits, leases and powers of attorney: County Clerk, Brenham.
  • Appraisal values and exemptions: the county appraisal district.
  • Tax certificates and tax bills: the county tax office.

Official Public Records are online through eDocTec, and deed records and official public records run from 1836 to the present. Use the index to find an instrument, then ask the clerk about copies.

Older records exist in other forms. The county's deed record for 1834 to 1904 is on microfilm held at Texas A&M University in College Station, with direct and reverse indexes on separate reels. Probate minutes, probate records, marriage records from 1837 and tax rolls from 1837 to 1910 are covered too. An old family farm may need that older chain of title when a buyer's title company starts its search.

  • Begin with the current owner's name and latest deed, then trace each deed of trust and release.
  • Look for liens, easements and affidavits recorded after the deed.
  • For a plat, ask the clerk for a copy, which costs $10.00.
  • For an inherited house, check for recorded estate instruments, covered below.

Page one costs $25.00, each page after that is $4.00, and each indexed name beyond five adds $0.25.

Washington County Clerk recording fees

Ask the clerk for the exact total on your document before you mail it. Send it to the Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, Brenham, TX 77833, with the correct filing fee. A plat also needs a current tax certificate showing no delinquent ad valorem taxes.

sections.h2: What a deed needs to be recorded
sections.html:
A deed must be an original, properly notarized or certified by the recording office of another county, state or country, and it must meet any requirements in Texas statute.

Property Code 12.001(b) makes a land conveyance recordable only when it is signed and acknowledged, either before an authorized officer such as a notary or before two subscribing witnesses. Recordable items include warranty, special warranty, quitclaim, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, plus releases, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. A missing grantee mailing address can add a $25 charge.

  • Use the original signed document, not a photocopy.
  • Get the signature acknowledged by a notary or another authorized officer.
  • Include the grantee's mailing address.
  • Send the fee for the first page, added pages and any extra names.

Commissioners courts may waive land recording fees for buyers in certain grant programs, so ask the clerk whether that applies to yours.

These show up as recorded instruments that connect the owner on the old deed to the heirs. Which instrument you need depends on whether the estate went through court.

Four tools matter at the recording counter. A transfer on death deed avoids probate when it is recorded ahead of the owner's death. A muniment of title uses the court order and the will. A small estate affidavit fits estates of $75,000 or less, apart from the homestead, and needs court approval. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement that a title company may refuse.

  • Administered estate: an executor's or administrator's deed.
  • Will without administration: a court order and the will.
  • Transfer on death deed: record an affidavit of death with the death certificate.
  • No court action: an affidavit of heirship, which a buyer may question.

Heirs are never added to the old deed. A new instrument is recorded.

A foreclosure notice is posted at the courthouse door and filed with the clerk at least 21 days before the sale.

The sale is a public auction in a county-designated area, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on a first Tuesday. After a default notice, a borrower generally has 20 days to reinstate. State tax liens work differently: the Comptroller files notice with the county clerk, who records it in the state tax lien book. A federal tax lien recorded with the clerk draws the $30.00 fee.

Ordinary property tax liens begin each January 1 and do not show up as recorded deeds. Ask the county tax office for a tax certificate before closing. Plats need one too.

Start by pulling the deed and each recorded lien for the address, then confirm every release was filed. Title staff will repeat that search, but spotting a gap yourself saves time.

  • Search the online index for the current deed, deeds of trust, releases and affidavits.
  • Confirm that the owner on the deed matches the person selling, or record the heirship instrument first.
  • Ask the county for a tax certificate and pay delinquent taxes from proceeds if needed.
  • Look for a posted foreclosure notice if a payment has been missed.
  • Check a plat if the lot was recently divided.

Whatever is recorded against the property will surface in the buyer's title search.

sections.h2: Filing by mail or in person
sections.html:
Before you send anything, check the page count, because every page after the first adds $4.00. Count the names that need indexing too, since each one past five adds $0.25. Enclose the grantee's mailing address and a check for the full amount. If you are unsure of the total, call the clerk and ask.

When you visit Brenham, bring the original deed, a notary's acknowledgment already completed, and payment. Plan for a call ahead of time if you need a plat copy or a tax lien filed. A title company can do all of this for you on closing day, which is how most sellers handle it.

sections.h2: Selling fast with a messy record
sections.html:
Gaps in the record need not kill a sale. A financed buyer's lender will want every lien released and every heir documented before funding. A cash buyer drops the lender, yet the title company still wants a clean chain before the deed is recorded in Brenham.

Estate house? Record the right instrument first. Old deed of trust with no release? Ask the lender for one. Behind on taxes? Get a tax certificate and plan to pay from proceeds. Finish these early and every kind of offer can be judged on the same timeline.

faqs.q: Which office takes deeds for recording in Washington County, Texas?
faqs.a: The Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, Brenham, TX 77833. Mail the original signed deed with the fee, which is $25.00 for the first page.

faqs.q: Can I search Washington County deed records online?
faqs.a: Yes, through eDocTec. Deed records and official public records are online from 1836 to the present.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a plat?
faqs.a: $70.00 per slide to file, and $10.00 for a copy. Filing also requires a tax certificate showing no delinquent ad valorem taxes.

faqs.q: Does Washington County record transfer on death deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, the clerk records deeds for the county. A transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies, with the clerk where the land sits.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the clerk's office?
faqs.a: Try 979-277-6216 for questions about the office. Ask about hours and recording in the same call.
